title: UART loop: the chip texts itself
warning: When done: move J16 and J17 back to XDS (right)
credit: Board drawing: TI SLAU869E, leader lines removed

label: Unplug USB. Move J16 and J17 to BP (left)
PA8 and PA9 are the chip's serial pins.
These two jumpers are a switch for where
those pins are connected:
XDS (right, as shipped): to the USB debug chip,
so the Mac can show the text the chip prints
BP (left): to the header pins, where your wire is
One wire: J1 pin 4 (PA8) to J1 pin 3 (PA9)
PA8 sends serial data (TX = transmit),
PA9 receives it (RX = receive).
Wired together, every byte the chip sends
comes straight back, so it can check them.
Then plug USB back in.

task_facts.head: For this test
items: Sends 2,048 random bytes at each speed and counts what comes back right
The Mac's serial window stays empty: the pins go to the wire, not the debug chip. Results are read over the debugger
Every byte right up to 4.5 Mbaud and from 6.4 to 10.67 Mbaud. 5 to 6 Mbaud fails, the same dead band as the larger MSPM0G3507 chip, so pick a speed outside it
